author: HaloGuardian101
body:
So I have seen some hackers on avicus but not much,

THE /STAFFLIST GONE! <-----

Most of the avicus players know what the command /stafflist is. 
For those who don't know /stafflist finds staff members who are online.

That's the problem. Hackers would know if moderators are on, so they wouldn't hack until the moderator/staff member leaves the server.
Then the problem begins, the hacker strikes until a moderator pops up on the server. They toggle their hacks on.

This is just a random idea I thought of to make the server more fun!

Thanks
-Halo

replies.author: Acceqted
replies.body:
I don't think I'm understanding your point here? Are you suggesting we toggle /staff ?


-EDIT- Ok, now I understand.



OT: I think /stafflist was meant for regulars to see which staff are online and so far that's what has worked. But with toggling /staff, wouldn't change much in my opinion just because of the hackers looking at tab. I feel that it's main purpose as I've stated before has helped the community so much, it's not worth cutting it out.

replies.author: GrapeSmoothie
replies.body: A large majority of hackers that join the server are new and aren't really aware of a /staff command. They hack and get banned and in the situation that a staff member is not on players can record and make a forum report. In the case that a player is aware a staff member is on which is a rare occasion unless they are a regular, staff members can just go to alternative accounts.

replies.author: hasl
replies.body:
There's no way to completely hide a staff member unless /vanish is used, because; as Venny said above; /who and /list (same command) will display who's in your rotation.
Therefore removing /stafflist would create an outcome with no positives, just negatives.
Thus this idea is will not work, also how would it be "more fun"  eh?

replies.author: Javipepe
replies.body:
I'd say roughly 1% of our hackers are actually aware of any of the custom commands we have like, for example, /staff or even /msg or /reply (some just like to type in global chat because don't know how to answer a message), /t, /settings, etc...

I don't think it's worth the hassle honestly, plus there is no immediate easy solution to it more than removing the command that is ultra-handy for regulars and people who actually know the server and for staff, too.
